title: Routing Evidence for Unseen Actions in Video Moment Retrieval

problem.claim: Video moment retrieval locates a video segment according to a query, but this work considers queries containing action types unseen during training.

gap.claim: Existing methods assume that training and testing samples share the same action types, which hinders real-world application.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Routing Evidence, a plug-and-play structure with multiple evidence-learning heads and a dynamic router for locating sentences containing unseen actions.
Each evidence-learning head estimates uncertainty while regressing timestamps, and the evidence distribution is formulated with a Normal-Inverse Gamma function.
A router selects the most appropriate evidence distribution for each sample.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors study the efficacy of Routing Evidence on three updated databases in which training and testing samples contain different action types.
The authors report that Routing Evidence outperforms other state-of-the-art methods with a more robust predictor.

narrative_sequence.summary: Video moment retrieval locates a video segment from a query.
Existing methods assume shared action types across training and testing, limiting real-world application.
The paper addresses video moment retrieval for queries with unseen actions.
Routing Evidence uses multiple uncertainty-aware evidence-learning heads and a router that selects an appropriate distribution for each sample.
The authors evaluate the method on three updated databases and report stronger performance than other state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: The method combines uncertainty estimation with dynamic routing among multiple evidence-learning heads.

interpretation.claim: Routing among uncertainty-aware predictors is presented as a way to handle action types unseen during training.

application.claim: This approach could be considered for retrieval systems facing differences between training and testing action types.

exception.claim: The abstract reports empirical evaluation on three updated databases but does not establish performance beyond those settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results or dataset names.
The abstract does not specify the evaluation protocol, baselines, or uncertainty-estimation details.
